reasoning_traces.think:
The core operation begins with scene segmentation, where full-resolution images are processed to locate objects such as players. This is followed by generation of a reduced-resolution image containing only the located objects, enabling efficient computation. The second phase involves detecting key points—such as limbs or body parts—on this reduced image. These points are mapped into a structured pose representation via a kernel function that encodes spatial relationships. The process leverages the fact that high-resolution detail is unnecessary for point localization, allowing real-time performance. Failure modes include misclassification during segmentation, insufficient resolution for accurate point detection, and invalid skeletal structures due to occlusion or noise. Dualities arise in the trade-off between computational load and accuracy: higher resolution improves precision but increases latency, while lower resolution accelerates processing but risks loss of detail. The system assumes consistent object types (e.g., humans), which enables template-based or learned prior models to guide inference.
